newsitem.title: USA: JAPAN READY TO ACT IN NEW ASIA CURRENCY CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN READY TO ACT IN NEW ASIA CURRENCY CRISIS.

text.p: The situation in Asia's currency markets has stabilized after the international bailout for Thailand, but Japan is ready to help if there is a new crisis, a Japanese international finance source said on Wednesday.

"There has been some contagion effect (from Thailand). I think the situation has stabilized for the time being. I do not see any immediate crisis in any other country, but we are ready to stand behind if any crisis might arise in the future," said the source, who asked not to be identified.
Many currencies in the Southeast Asia region came under pressure after one-time tiger economy Thailand was forced to devalue the baht last month.
The Philippines devalued the peso and sought $1 billion from the International Monetary Fund, while Indonesia widened the band in which the rupiah was allowed to trade against the dollar.
The IMF this week masterminded a $16 billion loan package to help Thailand out of its financial crisis. Japan and the IMF were the two biggest contributors to the package, offering $4 billion apiece.
